refresh_log.notes: Round 4, same day: prose and craft quality of the delivered markdown. Driven by counting defects in the first real AUDIT.md rather than by taste: 39 machine pluralisations ('13 dependency(ies) are unpinned'), 16 mid-string truncations that silently discarded information ('docs/api.md, docs/cli.md, docs/conc…' dropped two filenames), 11 lines of verbatim-repeated skip reasons, zero copy-pasteable commands, 5 checker internals leaking into prose, and no version stamp. Changes: (1) plural() and verb() helpers in _common.py, applied across 72 call sites in the 5 checkers with verb agreement moved to match -- this is why it was 72 hand edits and not a regex. Prose leaks removed at the same time: dropped '(ruff D1xx)' and '(1 difference(s))', and PKG-COMPETING-LINTERS now names the linter ('`black` is configured alongside ruff') instead of counting it. (2) Evidence moved to a collapsed appendix keyed by check ID; finding lines tease at most 2 items and cut at an ITEM boundary, never mid-string. rollup()'s default cap raised 8 -> 40 and 38 explicit small caps stripped, because a checker trimming to 8 made the appendix claim 'full detail' while holding back 48 paths. Appendix itself bounded at APPENDIX_ITEMS=15 with an explicit '…and N more': uncapped, ersilia produced a 504-line file (386 of it appendix), too much to leave in a repo root from a skill that flags verbose docs. Readable part (above the appendix) is 76-118 lines across all 7 calibration repos. (3) The Fix plan opens with a runnable fenced bash block of the AUTO commands, $SKILL declared once. Two correctness fixes found while building it: T0-FOOTER-DRIFT was prose inside a bash block so it moved out of AUTOFIX to EDIT, and the ruff commands now pass --config $SKILL/references/canonical-ruff.toml because a bare 'ruff check --fix .' would use the repo's own drifted config and fix something other than what the audit measured. Verified by running the pasted command with --diff on eosquality: 'Would fix 17 errors', matching the reported 17x I001, repo untouched. (4) AUTO/EDIT/ASK tag now also appears on the Findings line, sourced from build_fix_plan() so the two sections cannot drift. (5) Repeat-audit delta with THREE buckets -- fixed / no longer checked / new -- plus a <!-- checks-version --> footer stamp from _state.json. Two buckets would have lied: Tier 2 was gated in round 3, so a pre-gating report compared naively shows 8 items as 'fixed' when nothing was fixed. On stamp mismatch or absence the delta drops the word 'fixed' and says the comparison is indicative. Tier 2 is excluded from the delta on both sides because its roll-up line carries no recoverable IDs and every T2 item would otherwise read as 'new' every run -- found by asserting the parser could round-trip its own output, which it could not for T2. (6) Skip reasons grouped by reason instead of by id: 15 lines to 7. Regression gate: finding counts across all 7 calibration repos are IDENTICAL to the round-3 baseline, as intended for a wording-and-layout change. Bugs caught during this round: a dropped comma that silently merged a finding's summary and fix arguments, and a leftover 'break' from an earlier edit. Committed two worked examples under examples/ (eosquality: busy, 1 blocker, appendix, grouped skips; eos-python-package: quiet, 0 blockers, no appendix, template suppressions) plus an examples/README.md saying what to distrust first. Building the second example exposed two more real bugs: the Tier 2 roll-up read 'add a The README has no banner logo or badge row under the title' because it derived prose by slicing a summary that did not start with 'There is no' -- replaced with an explicit TIER2_LABEL table, the same reasoning as AREA_OF, after string-munging summaries produced garbage for the second time; and PKG-DEAD-MODULE-NAME flagged test_hello, since pytest discovers test functions BY NAME so a test_* function is never referenced and always looks dead -- check_dead_names now skips test modules. That false-positive fix is the only calibration change: eos-python-package 9 -> 8 should-fix, all six other repos identical.

Round 3, same day: report restructured, Tier 2 gated, CLI coherence added. (1) REPORT SHAPE. The first real AUDIT.md (eosquality, 206 lines / 35 findings) read badly for three measured reasons: 25 of 35 findings printed twice (once under a severity heading, again under Suggested remediation, ~56 wasted lines); severity-first grouping scattered related work (README problems across three sections) where area-grouping gives 9 groups of max 8; and the actionable section started at line 151 of 206. Rebuilt as three parts with distinct jobs -- Verdict (LLM prose via --verdict, area status table, --start-here), Findings by area (one line each: what is wrong and where, NO fix text), Fix plan (- [ ] checklist tagged AUTO/EDIT/ASK: what to do). That purpose split, not prose trimming, is what removes the duplication: 0 duplicated sentences now, verified programmatically. Reports are 93-132 lines across the 7 calibration repos. render_report.py owns AREA_OF (exact check id -> area; prefix matching was tried and misfiled PKG-DOCSTRING-* under Documentation) and AREA_TYPES. Status markers are data only (blocker/should-fix/nice-to-have/passed/not-run) -- no decorative emoji, since the skill flags T0-README-EMOJI elsewhere. The pass/not-run invariant broke TWICE in development: first marking a clean-but-partially-skipped area 'not checked', then marking an App repo's Tests & CI 'clean' when no test check had run (check_code only runs check_tests for Package/Template). Root cause: checkers emit one representative skip per gated group, not one per check, so 'was everything skipped?' is unanswerable from the skip list. Fixed with AREA_TYPES -- an area that does not apply to the type is omitted rather than marked, and an area with findings is always shown. (2) TIER 2 GATING. Nothing in T2 is unconditional now; ersilia is a very evolved package and is not the bar for a 7-commit script. CHANGELOG needs >=2 releases; CITATION needs a linked publication or a DOI/arXiv id in the README (--backs-paper for the Airtable signal); community files need >=3 contributors OR >=5 stars OR >=2 releases. The >=2-releases term is deliberate -- >=1 would have kept eosquality's block open on a single v0.0.1 tag. Verified live: closes for eosquality (1/1/1), opens for isaura, stylia, olinda, compound-embedding, ersilia-pack, lazy-qsar, ersilia. Gated checks are skipped WITH the numbers stated. Nice-to-have fell 9->2 (eosquality) and 11->4 (eos-python-package). (3) CLI COHERENCE. New references/canonical-cli.md plus an AST pass over Click and argparse. The canon was forked -- ersilia is 10 snake_case options against 8 kebab-case -- so kebab-case was ruled canonical (Click/POSIX norm; Click maps --batch-size to batch_size so only the flag string changes; ersilia's newer options already use it). Consequence accepted and reported, not special-cased: ersilia is non-compliant on 10 of its own options plus --output_file, and carries a typo, --nearest-neigbors. New checks: PKG-CLI-OPT-SEPARATOR, PKG-CLI-INCONSISTENT, PKG-CLI-VERB-DIVERGENT (near-synonyms of ersilia's 11 verbs; domain verbs like fit/build pass), PKG-CLI-IO-NAMING, PKG-CLI-NO-SHORT-IO. eosquality yields exactly one -- download -> fetch; its options were inspected directly and are already kebab-case with -i/-o pairs present, so a separator or short-IO finding there would be a false positive.

Round 2, same day: added the checks the user asked for after reviewing the first pass. New — Airtable Projects link and Type-vs-observed coincidence (T0-AIRTABLE-NO-PROJECT, T0-AIRTABLE-TYPE-MISMATCH, both LLM-checked in Step 2); README quality (T0-README-AI-TONE with a 37-term LLM-vocabulary list plus em-dash rate and bold-lead-in-bullet shape, T0-README-EMOJI, T0-README-NO-PURPOSE, T0-README-NO-ECOSYSTEM, T0-H1-NOT-DESCRIPTIVE); repo naming restricted to lowercase alphanumeric plus hyphens only, no underscores (T0-REPO-NAME); dependency declaration completeness (PKG-DEP-UNDECLARED, PKG-DEP-UNUSED with an import-name-to-distribution map); opt-in external link checking (T0-BROKEN-EXTERNAL-LINK, --check-external); and a whole new check_practices.py covering bad practices (bare excepts, print in library code, hardcoded absolute paths, shell=True, wildcard imports, mutable defaults, commented-out code, TODO density), modularity (god modules, long functions, deep nesting, flat namespace), messiness (root clutter, non-snake_case modules) and eosvc appropriateness. Output changed: the report is now AUDIT.md at the audited repo's root by default, always confirmed with the user first, and carries a Suggested-remediation section splitting the work into Blockers / mechanical-with-command / straightforward / judgement-required so it can be fed to a fixing session. SKILL.md gained a first-class 'Questions you must ask' section. AI-tone detector unit-tested against generated vs human README text: fires on the former (30 hits / 29 terms), silent on the latter. Redundancy checked against the Airtable registry: no existing repo audits repository contents; eosquality scores predictions, ersilia-maintenance and ersilia-model-workflows maintain model repos, eosvc syncs data, github-digest covers org-wide registry drift. Two more false positives fixed: a 0 KB data/example.csv is now Should-fix rather than Blocker (severity scales at 64 KB), and package fixture dirs are exempt from the size-based data check.

Initial buildout. Surveyed 179 Airtable Repositories records (141 public; Package 71, Analysis 69, Automation 14, Workshop 11, App 8, Template 5, Documentation 3) plus 20 repos read in detail: the 3 eos-* templates, eosquality, and 16 flagship/representative repos. Key findings driving the design: (1) the template CLAUDE.md files are the de-facto written spec and nothing enforces them; (2) compliance is low -- of 16 surveyed repos, 3 have a CLAUDE.md, 4 a ruff.toml, 4 tests, and only ersilia uses NumPy docstrings; (3) conventions have forked -- two incompatible ruff dialects, four About-Ersilia footer paragraphs, test/ vs tests/, src/ vs flat, pyproject vs requirements.txt vs nothing. Decisions taken with the user: canonical ruff = the ersilia dialect (only one enforcing convention=numpy); canonical footer = the eos-python-package/eos-analysis-template block (byte-identical in both, verified with od -c); report-only, never edits the target; type-aware profiles keyed on the Airtable Type; three tiers all reported with T2 labelled aspirational; the target repo's own CLAUDE.md overrides the profile where it explicitly differs, EXCEPT when it is a template leftover; eosNxxx model repos refused and delegated to ersilia-model-test / model-incorporation-*. Host has ruff at ~/miniconda3/bin/ruff but no uvx/pipx/vulture, so dead-code detection is stdlib-AST.
